run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Investigation of namespace social-network (authorized window 2026-11-20T17:35:40Z to 2026-11-21T17:35:40Z). Telemetry has only ~30 s of history (kube-state and Loki samples begin at 17:35:13-17:35:40Z), so the assessment rests on the current cluster state plus that live tail. The one failing workload is Deployment custom-service: its pod template (revision 3, generation 3) carries an init container named hang-init (busybox:1.36, '/bin/sh -c sleep infinity') that never exits, so all three pods custom-service-66f88bcc9c-{lpfcc,vvp7t,x5cwk} are Pending with Initialized=False (reason ContainersNotInitialized), the init container running since 17:35:23Z and custom-service-main waiting with reason PodInitializing; the Deployment reports replicas 3, unavailableReplicas 3, no ready replicas, and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available is 0 for custom-service while every other social-network deployment reads 1. The 27 social-network microservice deployments are up (pods Running/ready, restart count 0), no OOM events and all four nodes Ready, Jaeger traces show nginx-web-server /wrk2-api/post/compose and /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read returning http.status_code=200 in ~1.1-8.6 ms, and wrk2 round #0 reported 1024 requests in 10 s at 102.38 req/s. social-graph-service emitted continuous 'GetFollowers ... user_id: N not found' warnings (181 log lines total in the window, only 2 matching an error pattern), which is recorded as an unresolved data-level hypothesis because there is no populated-graph baseline. No request-path impact from the failing custom-service was observed: it has no Service and no traces.

claims.text: Deployment custom-service in namespace social-network has generation 3 and a pod template whose initContainers contain hang-init (image busybox:1.36, command ['/bin/sh','-c','sleep infinity']) alongside container custom-service-main (python:3.9-slim); the deployment's kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation contains no init container, so the init container is a later patch to the template.

All three custom-service pods in ReplicaSet custom-service-66f88bcc9c are phase Pending with condition Initialized=False/reason ContainersNotInitialized, init container hang-init in state running (startedAt 2026-11-21T17:35:23Z) and container custom-service-main waiting with reason PodInitializing: pods custom-service-66f88bcc9c-lpfcc, custom-service-66f88bcc9c-vvp7t, custom-service-66f88bcc9c-x5cwk.

Deployment custom-service status reports observedGeneration 3, replicas 3, unavailableReplicas 3 and no readyReplicas/availableReplicas value, with a Progressing condition stating ReplicaSet custom-service-66f88bcc9c is progressing.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_available at 2026-11-21T17:35:40Z is 0 for deployment custom-service and 1 for each of the other 27 social-network deployments (compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, social-graph-service, user-service, nginx-thrift, etc.).

The custom-service rollout added the hanging init container as a template change: ReplicaSet custom-service-5c68f797 (revision annotation 1) has no init container, while custom-service-5d95dbc564 (revision 2) and custom-service-66f88bcc9c (revision 3, 3 replicas) both carry hang-init; events record Deployment custom-service ScalingReplicaSet 5c68f797 0->3 at 17:35:20Z, 5c68f797 3->0 and 5d95dbc564 0->3 at 17:35:22Z, and 5d95dbc564 3->0 and 66f88bcc9c 0->3 at 17:35:23Z, with SuccessfulDelete of the earlier pods.

Every social-network application pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and start times between 17:35:13Z and 17:35:18Z, while the three custom-service-66f88bcc9c pods are the only Pending pods in the namespace (all 33 pods listed).

Jaeger spans in 17:35:22-17:35:40Z show the Social Network request path succeeding: nginx-web-server /wrk2-api/post/compose spans carry http.status_code=200 with durations 7.5-8.6 ms and /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read spans carry http.status_code=200 with durations 1.1-1.5 ms, with downstream compose-post-service, social-graph-service (get_followers_server 1.1 ms), home-timeline-service, post-storage-service, text-service and user-service spans showing no error tags and no error status.

The load generator log for wrk2 round #0 against http://10.96.210.33:8080/wrk2-api/post/compose records 1024 requests in 10.00s, Requests/sec 102.38 and Transfer/sec 20.05KB, i.e. the front end answered the load without a reported transport failure during that round.

social-graph-service logged continuous warnings of the form '(SocialGraphHandler.h:612:GetFollowers) user_id: <id> not found' between 17:35:35Z and 17:35:39Z (50 newest lines all of that form, including user_id 1), and the service produced 181 log lines in the window of which only 2 matched an error pattern (the two startup index-creation errors).

Startup-time MongoDB errors were transient: user-service, user-timeline-service and social-graph-service logged 'Error in createIndexes: No suitable servers found' / 'Failed to create mongodb index, try again' between 17:35:14Z and 17:35:18Z, after which each logged 'Starting the <service> server' and no further index errors; the same pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts.

Service configuration is uniform and contains no fault/delay/error settings: configmaps compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, social-graph-service and user-timeline-service all hold the same generic service-config.json with the expected hostnames/ports (e.g. social-graph-service:9090, social-graph-mongodb:27017, social-graph-redis:6379) and 10000 ms timeouts.

Alert state read at 17:36:09Z (after the authorized window end) shows rules PodStatusError (reason PodInitializing), PendingPodsDetected and KubePodNotReady pending for custom-service-66f88bcc9c-lpfcc, -vvp7t and -x5cwk, while HighRequestErrorRate, HighRequestLatency, DeploymentNotReady and ContainerCPUThrottling carry no alerts.

Deployment custom-service has no Service and no Endpoints object (30 Services and 26 Endpoints exist in social-network and none selects app=custom-service), so the failing deployment is not on the observed request path; Services/Endpoints for all 26 Social Network backends have matching selectors and populated addresses.

The custom-service pods are not blocked by resource pressure or node problems: all four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) are Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure False, all three pods carry PodScheduled=True, and container_oom_events_total is 0 for every social-network container at the 17:35:40Z sample.

The pervasive social-graph-service 'GetFollowers ... user_id not found' warnings may mean the social-graph store holds no user/follower data, so home-timeline writes and reads resolve to no followers; the evidence available cannot confirm this is abnormal because there is no baseline scrape or log sample from before 17:35:13Z and the observed load (post/compose and home-timeline/read) shows no user-registration traffic that would populate the graph.

Custom-service pods being stuck is not explained by MongoDB/DNS unavailability of a dependency: their main container never starts (init phase never completes), the pods are scheduled on sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3, and no custom-service pod emitted a startup connection error; the MongoDB connection-refused errors observed at 17:35:14-18Z belonged to user-service, user-timeline-service and social-graph-service and stopped after their databases came up.

Remove the hang-init init container from Deployment custom-service (or replace its command '/bin/sh -c sleep infinity' with one that completes) so the three pending pods can initialize and the deployment can reach its 3 desired available replicas; then confirm kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="social-network",deployment="custom-service"} reaches 3 and the PodInitializing/PendingPodsDetected alerts clear.

gaps: Change history is not integrated (not_integrated: change_history), so which actor or controller added the hang-init init container to Deployment custom-service, and the exact patch body for revisions 2 and 3, are unknown; only the last-applied annotation (no init container) and the three ReplicaSet revisions show that the template changed.

Telemetry history is effectively absent before the incident tail: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available, container_oom_events_total and other Prometheus series return a single sample at 2026-11-21T17:35:40Z, and Loki lines only from about 17:35:13Z, so no pre-incident baseline exists for error rate, latency or pod state, and nothing can be said about earlier state in the 24 h window.

Events show every social-network deployment scaling its ReplicaSet from 0 to 1 between 17:35:13Z and 17:35:18Z (all application pods start in that interval with restartCount 0); the cause of that namespace-wide (re)deployment is unknown and, with no change history, it cannot be attributed to the custom-service fault or ruled out as the incident trigger.

fetch_pod_logs was denied (HTTP 403 SOURCE_FORBIDDEN) for pod wrk2-job-gqld7, so container logs could not be read through the Kubernetes API; log evidence comes only from Loki, which retains just the last ~30 s.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_* exist as metric names but return no series for the authorized window (get_series/instant increase returned no data), so per-service span error-rate and latency metrics could not be used; only the biased Jaeger samples and log counts support the health statements.

The wrk2 load-generator Job/pod is no longer present in the cluster (no Jobs or app=wrk2-job pods in social-network at query time), so its full round sequence and whether later rounds exercised read paths differently is unknown.

Whether custom-service is intended as part of the Social Network application could not be verified: it has no Service, no Endpoints, no traces and no relation to the microservice configmaps, and its only linkage to the application is the social-network namespace.

The social-graph 'user_id not found' pattern cannot be judged abnormal or normal without a populated-graph baseline; if the graph store is expected to be pre-populated, its contents would need to be checked (MongoDB/Redis data is not observable through the available tools).
next_steps: Human review of the change record for Deployment custom-service (who added initContainers[hang-init] with 'sleep infinity' and why) once a change-history source is available.
Confirm with the application owner whether Deployment custom-service belongs to the Social Network stack or is an unrelated workload sharing the namespace.

If social-graph lookups are expected to succeed, verify the social-graph-mongodb / social-graph-redis contents for user and follower data and compare against a known-good deployment before attributing the GetFollowers warnings to a defect.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
